title: Medium Layered Hair With Curtain Bangs
description: Medium layered hair with curtain bangs gives you body, movement, and a face-framing shape that works on many hair types. The length usually sits around the shoulders, with soft layers through the mid-lengths and ends to keep the cut from looking heavy or blocky. Curtain bangs are cut longer at the outer corners and slightly shorter near the center part, so they open around your eyes and cheekbones instead of sitting flat on your forehead. This combination is ideal if your hair feels flat or lifeless, because the layers help create lift and the fringe adds interest without a dramatic chop. Style with a round brush and blow-dryer for a smooth, polished finish, or add a light texturizing spray for a more relaxed, lived-in look that still feels put together.
whyWeLoveIt: Maximum volume and lightened ends for dense or heavy hair
stylingTip: Mist root booster spray before blow-drying upside down for instant height.

title: Shoulder Length Hair With Curtain Bangs
description: Shoulder length hair with curtain bangs is a classic, easy-to-wear option that suits a wide range of face shapes and ages. The hair usually grazes the shoulders or hits just above, which is long enough for ponytails and buns but short enough to feel fresh and manageable. Curtain bangs add softness around the face and help break up a strong jawline or broad forehead, especially when they’re cut to skim the cheekbones or the top of the nose. This look can be worn sleek and straight with a blowout, softly waved for everyday, or curled for more volume at the crown. Using a small to medium round brush on the bangs, directing them away from the face, creates that signature salon-style swoop that frames your features without feeling stiff.
whyWeLoveIt: Effortless movement that frames the face beautifully
stylingTip: Blow-dry with a 1.5-inch round brush away from your face and set with a light texturizing spray.

title: Medium Shag Haircut With Curtain Bangs
description: A medium shag haircut with curtain bangs is perfect if you like texture, movement, and a slightly undone finish. The cut features choppy, layered lengths around the crown and through the mid-lengths, which remove weight and create natural volume even on finer hair. Curtain bangs are usually cut a bit thicker in shag haircuts so they blend into the shorter layers around the face, giving that rock-inspired, tousled shape that still feels modern. This look is especially flattering on wavy or slightly curly textures because the layers encourage your natural bend and keep the shape from looking bulky. To style, apply a lightweight mousse or texture spray on damp hair, diffuse or air-dry, then use your fingers to break up the waves, focusing on lifting the bangs at the root so they open up your face.
whyWeLoveIt: Maximum volume and lightened ends for dense or heavy hair
stylingTip: Mist root booster spray before blow-drying upside down for instant height.

title: Medium Lob Haircut With Curtain Bangs
description: A medium lob haircut with curtain bangs gives you that in-between length that feels chic but still easy to manage. The lob usually falls somewhere between the collarbone and the top of the shoulders, offering enough length to tuck behind your ears or put into a half-up style. Curtain bangs add softness to the front and prevent the classic lob shape from feeling too blunt or severe, especially on straight hair. They also help visually slim the face by drawing the eye inward towards your eyes and cheekbones. This look works with smooth, sleek blowouts for a polished finish or with loose waves for a more relaxed, everyday style; using a heat protectant and a medium-barrel curling iron on random sections will give that effortless bend that pairs nicely with the parted fringe.
whyWeLoveIt: Effortless movement that frames the face beautifully
stylingTip: Blow-dry with a 1.5-inch round brush away from your face and set with a light texturizing spray.

title: Medium Wavy Hair With Curtain Bangs
description: Medium wavy hair with curtain bangs creates a soft, romantic look that feels effortless and very current. The mid-length cut allows your waves to fall and bounce without weighing them down, while the bangs frame the face and blend seamlessly into the front layers. Curtain bangs on wavy hair usually work best when cut slightly longer, so they follow the natural bend instead of fighting it. To style, many stylists suggest air-drying or using a diffuser to define your waves, then shaping the bangs with a round brush or simply twisting them back while they dry to encourage that curtain effect. A light curl cream or wave spray helps reduce frizz and keep the bang area from puffing up, so you get soft, defined movement that still looks natural and touchable.
whyWeLoveIt: Relaxed model-off-duty texture that looks great air-dried
stylingTip: Scrunch with sea salt spray on 80% dry hair for natural beachy bends.

title: Medium Straight Hair With Curtain Bangs
description: Medium straight hair with curtain bangs looks clean, sleek, and modern while still feeling soft around the face. The medium length gives straight hair enough weight to sit smoothly, but the fringe prevents it from appearing too flat or one-dimensional. Curtain bangs on straight hair often need a bit of styling to maintain their swoop, so a blow-dryer and small round brush or a flat iron are useful tools. You can bend the bangs slightly away from the face so they curve around your eyes and cheeks, rather than falling straight down. A smoothing cream or light serum on the mid-lengths and ends keeps everything glossy and frizz-free, while a small amount of volumizing spray at the roots stops the bangs from separating or looking limp throughout the day.
whyWeLoveIt: Sleek, glossy contrast that brings structure to facial features
stylingTip: Finish with a drop of weightless hair oil to tame flyaways and boost shine.

title: Thick Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs
description: Thick medium hair with curtain bangs can look full and luxurious when cut and shaped properly. The key is adding internal layers that remove some weight without making the ends look thin, so the hair still feels dense but moves easily. Curtain bangs help break up heavy front sections by adding a shorter, face-framing focal point that softens the hairline and prevents that “wall of hair” feeling. A slightly longer curtain bang works best on thick hair so it blends into the surrounding layers and does not puff out. To style, use a round brush to smooth the bangs and front pieces while blow-drying, then apply a light smoothing cream through the mid-lengths and ends; if you want extra movement, finish with a large-barrel curling iron just on the outer layers to create loose, bouncy bends.
whyWeLoveIt: Effortless movement that frames the face beautifully
stylingTip: Blow-dry with a 1.5-inch round brush away from your face and set with a light texturizing spray.

title: Fine Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs
description: Fine medium hair with curtain bangs benefits from smart cutting and lightweight products that create the illusion of volume. A blunt or slightly textured perimeter at the shoulders helps make fine strands look fuller at the bottom, while soft, face-framing layers keep everything from appearing too wispy. Curtain bangs bring attention to your eyes and cheekbones and can make the front look thicker, especially if the fringe is cut with a bit of density near the part. Avoid over-thinning the bangs or the ends, as that can make the hair look even finer. For styling, a volumizing mousse at the roots, a round brush blowout on the bangs, and a quick bent pass with a flat iron on the mid-lengths will give you soft lift and movement without weighing the hair down with heavy creams or oils.
whyWeLoveIt: Effortless movement that frames the face beautifully
stylingTip: Blow-dry with a 1.5-inch round brush away from your face and set with a light texturizing spray.

title: Medium Layered Bob With Curtain Bangs
description: A medium layered bob with curtain bangs is a great choice if you want a structured shape with soft, face-framing movement. The bob length usually sits around the collarbone or slightly above, with layers through the interior to prevent a bulky, triangular silhouette. Curtain bangs open up the front and keep the bob from feeling too sharp, adding a romantic touch to an otherwise clean cut. This look is especially flattering on oval, round, and heart-shaped faces because the fringe and layers can be customized to balance different features. Style with a smooth blowout for a sleek, professional vibe or add soft waves with a curling iron for a more relaxed finish; always shape the bangs first, directing them away from your face so they fall like drapes on either side of your part.
whyWeLoveIt: Maximum volume and lightened ends for dense or heavy hair
stylingTip: Mist root booster spray before blow-drying upside down for instant height.

title: Curly Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs
description: Curly medium hair with curtain bangs creates a bold, expressive look with lots of personality. The mid-length cut keeps curls bouncy and easier to manage than very long hair, while removing enough weight so the curl pattern can spring up. Curtain bangs on curly hair are typically cut dry or slightly stretched so your stylist can see exactly where each curl will fall around your face. The fringe often sits around cheekbone to jaw length when the curls bounce up, creating a soft curtain effect instead of a short, straight-across bang. To style, apply a curl cream or gel to damp hair, diffuse with low heat, and gently separate the bang curls with your fingers once dry; avoid heavy blowouts that might disturb the curl structure and cause frizz around the fringe.
whyWeLoveIt: Accentuates natural coil bounce while lifting crown volume
stylingTip: Apply hydrating curl cream on soaking wet hair and diffuse on low heat.

title: Medium Hair With Long Curtain Bangs
description: Medium hair with long curtain bangs gives you maximum flexibility because the fringe can be pushed back, tucked behind the ears, or styled forward. These bangs are usually cut to hit somewhere between the cheekbones and the jawline, so they read more like face-framing layers than traditional bangs. On shoulder-length hair, long curtain bangs help slim the face by drawing the eye inward and creating soft angles along the sides of your cheeks. They work well on straight, wavy, and curly textures, especially if you want something low-commitment that grows out gracefully. Style them by blow-drying with a small round brush, flipping the ends away from the face, or use a flat iron to bend them slightly back; finishing with a light-hold spray keeps them in place without making the hair stiff or crunchy.
whyWeLoveIt: Low commitment fringe that grows out seamlessly into layers
stylingTip: Use velcro rollers on damp crown sections while doing makeup for extra bounce.

title: Medium Hair With Wispy Curtain Bangs
description: Medium hair with wispy curtain bangs has a soft, airy look that feels light and easy. Wispy bangs are cut with less density and more texture, so small pieces fall lightly across your forehead and gradually blend into the longer hair on the sides. On medium lengths, this creates movement and dimension without blocking your features or feeling heavy. Wispy curtain bangs are a great choice if you are nervous about committing to a thicker fringe but still want that face-framing shape. To style, use minimal product—usually just a light volumizing spray or a touch of mousse at the roots—and blow-dry the bangs with your fingers or a small brush, lifting them up and away from the face for a soft, piecey effect that looks effortless.
whyWeLoveIt: Low commitment fringe that grows out seamlessly into layers
stylingTip: Use velcro rollers on damp crown sections while doing makeup for extra bounce.

title: Medium Hair With Blunt Curtain Bangs
description: Medium hair with blunt curtain bangs combines a stronger bang line with the signature parted shape. Instead of wispy or heavily textured fringe, blunt curtain bangs have a bit more weight and a clearer edge while still being longer at the sides and slightly shorter in the center. On shoulder-length hair, this creates a bold frame around the eyes and can add structure to softer or more delicate facial features. The rest of the cut can stay mostly one length or feature subtle layers to keep it from appearing too boxy. For styling, a smooth blowout is key: use a round brush and blow-dryer to direct the bangs down and then out to each side, finishing with a light smoothing serum to keep the fringe polished and free from frizz throughout the day.
whyWeLoveIt: Sleek, glossy contrast that brings structure to facial features
stylingTip: Finish with a drop of weightless hair oil to tame flyaways and boost shine.

title: Medium Hair With Side Curtain Bangs
description: Medium hair with side curtain bangs is a good option if you prefer a side part but love the face-framing effect of this fringe. Instead of parting directly down the middle, the bangs are cut to sweep out from a slightly off-center or deeper side part, still opening away from the face on both sides. On a shoulder-length cut, this creates asymmetry that can help balance features like a strong jaw or a more prominent forehead. The rest of the hair can be softly layered to support the movement of the fringe and keep the overall shape from feeling lopsided. To style, blow-dry the bangs in the opposite direction of your part first to build volume at the root, then flip them back into place and use a small round brush to shape the ends so they sweep out gently.
whyWeLoveIt: Effortless movement that frames the face beautifully
stylingTip: Blow-dry with a 1.5-inch round brush away from your face and set with a light texturizing spray.

title: Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs And Layers
description: Medium hair with curtain bangs and layers is one of the most versatile combos because it adds movement, volume, and shape all at once. Layers throughout the mid-lengths and ends prevent the cut from looking heavy, while the bangs frame your features and tie the whole haircut together. This look works for straight, wavy, and curly hair and can be customized to suit different face shapes by adjusting where the layers start and how long the fringe falls. For example, higher cheekbone-grazing bangs and shorter layers around the front can lift and open up round or square faces. Style with a round brush and blow-dryer for smooth volume, or use a curling iron or wand to add loose waves through the mid-lengths; finishing with a texture spray will enhance the layered effect without weighing hair down.
whyWeLoveIt: Effortless movement that frames the face beautifully
stylingTip: Blow-dry with a 1.5-inch round brush away from your face and set with a light texturizing spray.

title: Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs And Soft Waves
description: Medium hair with curtain bangs and soft waves has that relaxed, everyday look many people want from salon inspiration photos. The hair usually hits around the shoulders with minimal or moderate layering, allowing the waves to fall in loose, flowing bends. Curtain bangs sit at cheekbone or nose length and blend gently into the surrounding layers so they move together with the rest of the haircut. This look works well on natural waves or can be created with a curling iron on straight hair. To style, apply a heat protectant, curl random sections away from the face, leave the ends slightly straighter for a modern feel, and then shape the bangs with a round brush or flat iron bend; finish by lightly brushing through the waves and adding a soft-hold spray for touchable movement.
whyWeLoveIt: Relaxed model-off-duty texture that looks great air-dried
stylingTip: Scrunch with sea salt spray on 80% dry hair for natural beachy bends.

title: Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs And Balayage
description: Medium hair with curtain bangs and balayage combines a flattering cut with dimension-boosting color. Balayage highlights are painted on for a soft, blended look that brightens the mid-lengths and ends while keeping the roots more natural. On shoulder-length hair, this technique adds depth and movement, making the layers and curtain bangs stand out more clearly. Lighter pieces around the face, often called “money pieces,” can be placed to accentuate the framing created by the bangs and draw attention to your eyes. To maintain the color and cut, use sulfate-free shampoo, regular deep conditioning, and schedule trim and touch-up appointments every few months; styling with a smooth blowout or loose waves will showcase both the shape of the haircut and the subtle transitions in color.
whyWeLoveIt: Dimensional face-framing money pieces that brighten skin tone
stylingTip: Use color-protecting sulfate-free shampoo to preserve highlight radiance.

title: Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs And Highlights
description: Medium hair with curtain bangs and highlights adds brightness and contrast without the commitment of an all-over dye job. Traditional foiled highlights or soft, blended streaks can be placed throughout the mid-lengths and ends to create dimension and the illusion of thicker hair. Adding slightly lighter pieces around the face works especially well with curtain bangs, because the fringe frames your features and the color emphasizes that framing. This combination is flattering on many skin tones when the highlight shade is chosen to complement your natural base color. To care for highlighted hair, use color-safe products, limit high-heat styling, and consider a purple or blue shampoo if you wear cool blonde or brunette shades; styling with a simple blowout or gentle waves will help the different tones catch the light and show off the movement of your cut.
whyWeLoveIt: Dimensional face-framing money pieces that brighten skin tone
stylingTip: Use color-protecting sulfate-free shampoo to preserve highlight radiance.

title: Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs And Low Maintenance Cut
description: Medium hair with curtain bangs and a low maintenance cut is perfect if you want something that looks styled without a lot of daily effort. The overall shape usually features a simple, slightly layered shoulder-length cut that air-dries well, paired with curtain bangs that grow out softly instead of needing constant trims. These bangs are typically cut a bit longer so they can be pushed to the sides, tucked behind your ears, or blended into face-framing layers if you skip a trim. The medium length is easy to wash, dry, and throw into a quick ponytail or clip when needed. For styling, focus on quick touches: blow-dry just the bangs with a round brush to set the shape, apply a lightweight cream or spray to the rest of your hair, and let your natural texture do the rest for a lived-in, effortless look.
whyWeLoveIt: Quick 5-minute styling routine perfect for busy mornings
stylingTip: Tuck behind ears on rush days; the soft fringe still frames jawlines perfectly.

title: Medium Hair With Curtain Bangs And Easy Styling
description: Medium hair with curtain bangs and easy styling focuses on simple routines and versatile looks you can switch up quickly. The haircut usually combines shoulder-length hair with soft layers and a fringe tailored to your texture, so it behaves well whether you blow-dry, air-dry, or use hot tools. Curtain bangs are cut to a length that still looks good on off days, even if you only give them a quick refresh with a brush or iron. You can wear the hair straight, add loose waves, or pull it half-up without losing the face-framing effect of the bangs. A few key products—like a heat protectant, light-hold mousse, and texturizing spray—are enough to create multiple finishes, from polished to tousled, making this combination ideal if you want a stylish haircut that fits into a busy routine.
whyWeLoveIt: Quick 5-minute styling routine perfect for busy mornings
stylingTip: Tuck behind ears on rush days; the soft fringe still frames jawlines perfectly.
